concepts.name: Laws of reflection
concepts.description: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection, and the incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in one plane.

concepts.name: Spherical mirrors & image formation
concepts.description: Concave and convex mirrors form real or virtual images depending on the object position.

concepts.name: Mirror formula, sign convention & magnification
concepts.description: Use the Cartesian sign convention with 1/v + 1/u = 1/f and m = -v/u.

concepts.name: Refraction & refractive index
concepts.description: Light bends when its speed changes between media; n = c/v.

concepts.name: Lenses & image formation
concepts.description: Convex and concave lenses converge or diverge light to form images.

concepts.name: Lens formula & power of a lens
concepts.description: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f and power P = 1/f (f in metres), measured in dioptres.

concepts.name: Human eye & accommodation
concepts.description: The eye lens changes its focal length to focus near and far objects on the retina.

concepts.name: Defects of vision & correction
concepts.description: Myopia, hypermetropia and presbyopia are corrected with suitable lenses.

concepts.name: Refraction through prism & dispersion
concepts.description: A prism splits white light into its component colours because each colour bends by a different amount.

concepts.name: Atmospheric refraction & scattering
concepts.description: Twinkling, advanced sunrise, the blue sky and red sunsets come from refraction and scattering in the atmosphere.

concepts.name: Electric charge & current
concepts.description: Current is the rate of flow of charge through a conductor.

concepts.name: Potential difference
concepts.description: Potential difference is the work done per unit charge in moving it between two points.

concepts.name: Ohm's law & resistance
concepts.description: At constant temperature, current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference across it.

concepts.name: Factors affecting resistance (resistivity)
concepts.description: Resistance grows with length, falls with cross-section area and depends on the material.

concepts.name: Resistors in series
concepts.description: Same current through each resistor; voltages add; total resistance is the sum.

concepts.name: Resistors in parallel
concepts.description: Same voltage across each branch; currents add; total resistance is less than the smallest branch.

concepts.name: Heating effect & electric power
concepts.description: Electrical energy turns into heat in a resistor; power is the rate of energy use.

concepts.name: Magnetic field & field lines
concepts.description: Field lines show the direction and strength of a magnetic field; they never cross.

concepts.name: Magnetic field due to current (wire, loop, solenoid)
concepts.description: A current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field around it (Oersted); a solenoid behaves like a bar magnet.

concepts.name: Force on current-carrying conductor (Fleming's LHR)
concepts.description: The force is perpendicular to both the current and the magnetic field; Fleming's left-hand rule gives its direction.

concepts.name: Domestic electric circuits & safety
concepts.description: Live, neutral and earth wires; fuses and earthing protect from overload and shocks.
